body: Reverse factoring (bank pays supplier early, company pays bank late) keeps the liability in trade payables and inflates CFO by the stretch; non-recourse factoring moves receivables to cash inside CFO. Disclosure: US ASU 2022-04 (from FY2023, XBRL tag SupplierFinanceProgramObligation; 87 filers tagged it at CY2025Q4, Walmart $6.0bn largest); IAS 7/IFRS 7 amendments (May 2023, effective 2024) and matching Ind AS 7/107 amendments - read the 'supplier finance arrangements' note. Worked example ADVANCE AUTO PARTS (10-K 0001193125-26-051305, $m): FY2023 payables 3,526 of which supplier finance 3,400 (~96%); payable days ~241 on continuing COGS 5,349; programme shrank to 2,500 by FY2025 while CFO went 287 -> 85 -> -46. Tests: supplier-finance obligations / trade payables (>30% red); DPO far above peers; a shrinking programme = coming cash outflow. Treat SF obligations as debt in net debt/EBITDA. Same family: First Brands 2025 off-balance-sheet receivable/inventory finance.
title: Supplier finance and factoring: CFO that is really debt (Advance Auto Parts)
